questions.text: How do two setN(x => x + 1) calls in one effect differ from two setN(n + 1) calls?
options: The function sees the update already queued. Both setN(n + 1) calls close over the same n
They do not differ. Both forms end on the same value
setN(n + 1) sees a fresher n than the function does
The function form is forbidden inside an effect

questions.text: How many extra renders do setA and setB produce when called one after another in one effect?
options: Two. Each setter renders on its own
One. Updates from the same effect fold into one render
None, until the whole effect and a timer finish
Three: after the effect and after each setter

questions.text: Why keep a value that is fully derived from props out of state?
options: State may not be read in a component that also has props
Props arrive after state, so the copy is always fresher
State remembers the first value and does not follow later props. Compute it during render
React resets that state on every render

questions.text: When does the useEffect body run relative to the component function?
options: Before return, along with the rest of the body
Instead of render, if the dependency array is empty
Only on a click, even with no handler
After the render has been committed. Not while the component function is running

questions.text: What does an empty effect dependency array do?
options: Keeps the run to mount. Later renders do not repeat this effect
Prevents the first run
Repeats the effect on every render
Runs the effect before the component function

questions.text: When does an effect cleanup run?
options: Right after the component return, before the effect
Before the next run of this effect and on unmount. It does not run before the very first run
Only if the dependency array is empty
Before every render, even with no effect

options: In the render body, next to return
In a useEffect with no dependency array
In the event handler. An effect after render does not know that a click happened
In the useState initial value

questions.text: Why can setItem(item) after item.n = 2 fail to produce a new render?
options: Mutating an object is blocked and the setter is discarded
The n field is not part of state, so no render is needed
An effect is not allowed to call a setter

questions.text: setA and setB in one effect always produce two separate extra renders.
A child’s useEffect runs before the parent’s useEffect.
Cleanup runs before the effect’s very first run.
A fresh object in the dependency array counts as a change on every render.
A component that did not mount still runs its useEffect.

A controlled field shows the text from state through value.
What runs first: the component body or its useEffect?
questions.answer: The component body. The effect runs after that render.

questions.text: What final n do two setN(n + 1) calls in one effect produce when n is 0 in that render?
questions.answer: 1. Both calls close over 0 and set 1. There is one extra render.

questions.text: What final n do two setN(x => x + 1) calls in one effect produce when n is 0?
questions.answer: 2. The second function sees the 1 queued by the first.

questions.text: Which dependency array keeps an effect to mount only?
questions.answer: An empty array []. With no array, the effect runs after every render.

questions.text: How does React compare values in a dependency array?
questions.answer: With Object.is. A new object on every render is a different dependency.

questions.text: Where do you keep a number that is fully derived from props?
questions.answer: Compute it during render. A copy in state stays on the first value.

questions.text: Why does an effect with no dependency array loop if every run calls setState?
questions.answer: The state update renders the component again, and that render runs the effect again.

questions.text: What happens to a request that should run only after a click if you put it in render?
questions.answer: It fires during render, with no click. A click needs a handler.
